characterization_methods.key_findings: After 1 h at 550 °C, there is no intensity difference between {111} and {200} reflections; ferrite is fully ordered DO3; dark-field image shows bright equiaxed ordered domains a few tens of nanometres across separated by dark boundaries; indexed reflections 000, 0-22, 1̄11, 2̄00, 400.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Diffraction pattern of ferrite in the [011]α zone axis (text also describes [110] zone axis); dark-field image using the {200} reflection; 100 nm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe ferrite structure modifications (ordering) during aging at 550 °C
characterization_methods.technique: TEM (transmission electron microscopy); selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) + dark-field imaging

interfaces.interface_notes: The ordered structures are not only due to the high level of aluminum of the steel but also due to partitioning between austenite and ferrite that leads to a level of Al in ferrite higher than the nominal composition.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Ferrite evolves to a fully ordered DO3 structure after 1 h aging at 550 °C; no intensity difference between {111} and {200} reflections remains.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent solution treatment (proc_st-850c-10min-wq) preceding the 550 °C/1 h aging step.
Aging at 550 °C for 1 h; ferrite becomes a fully ordered DO3 structure.

phases_present.morphology: bright equiaxed ordered domains a few tens of nanometres across, separated by dark boundaries

microstructure_list.region: ferrite phase (α) - dark-field TEM image using the {200} reflection

structures.overall_structure: Ferrite phase becomes a fully ordered DO3 structure after 1 h aging at 550 °C; dark-field TEM using the {200} reflection shows bright equiaxed ordered domains a few tens of nanometres across, separated by dark boundaries.

unmapped_findings: The as-quenched (pre-aging) ferrite of the same 29Mn-9.6Al-0.56C (wt.%) alloy (Fig. 9a) already exhibits a mix of B2- and DO3-ordered structures, as indicated by the intensity difference between {111} and {200} superlattice reflections; this is the starting state before the 550 °C/1 h aging that produces the fully ordered DO3 structure (context for the aged sample, Fig. 9b).
